title: Domain Registrations Auto-Renew Service Terms
content:
## Auto-renew service terms for Domain Registrations

1. **Who is renewed.** Auto-renew runs only for a domain whose auto-renew setting is on. Auto-renew is switched on or off according to the TLD's auto-renew default on every new registration and inbound transfer.
2. **Status.** An auto-renew charge may be attempted only while the domain status is active or on hold.
3. **Attempt calendar.** The first attempt runs on the day that lies the TLD's first-attempt number of calendar days before the expiry date. If it is declined, retries run on each of the TLD's retry days before the expiry date, and every declined attempt is recorded with its attempt number.
4. **Price and booking.** Each attempt renews the TLD's auto-renew term in years at the price set by the renewal charge terms, and is booked as an auto-renew charge.
5. **Funding.** The funding sources are tried in the TLD's auto-renew funding order. Account credit is used only if the credit balance covers the whole amount; otherwise the default card is charged. A charge is never split between sources.
6. **End of the cycle.** Once the last scheduled retry has declined — that is, once the declined attempts recorded in the current cycle equal one plus the number of retry days — no further automatic attempt is made in that cycle, and the domain expires normally on its expiry date, after which it can still be renewed manually during the renewal grace period. The current cycle runs from the first attempt day up to and including the domain's current expiry date.
7. **Switching the setting.** Switching auto-renew off stops the remaining attempts of the cycle but never reverses a charge already made. Switching it on after the first attempt day makes the next scheduled retry day the next attempt.

### Basis

The setting in clause 1 and the status in clause 2 are read from the system record of the domain holding before an attempt. The decline count in clause 6 is the number of declined auto-renew attempts recorded for that domain within the current cycle.

### Hypothetical illustration (invented calendar)

Take a TLD whose first attempt is 30 days before expiry and whose retry days are 14, 7 and 1 days before expiry. With four declined attempts recorded in the cycle — the first and all three retries — the count equals one plus three, so no further automatic attempt is made and the domain expires on its expiry date. If auto-renew is switched on 20 days before expiry, the next attempt is the retry 14 days before expiry.

### Questions the terms answer

- *Does switching auto-renew off refund a charge already taken?* No; it only stops the remaining attempts of the cycle.
- *Can part of an auto-renew charge come from account credit and the rest from the card?* No; account credit is used only when it covers the whole amount, and a charge is never split.
